stem: A 9-month-old had no obvious symptoms the first time egg was offered, but developed urticaria within minutes on a later exposure. Which immune event most plausibly occurred during the earlier sensitisation phase?

options.text: A macrophage presented the allergen to a Th2 cell, which stimulated a B cell to produce IgE
Neutrophils produced allergen-specific IgE immediately after ingestion
Complement activation caused delayed eosinophilic infiltration of the oesophagus
Pre-existing mast cells produced IgE before any allergen presentation occurred
The first exposure directly caused non-IgE-mediated disease without prior sensitisation

explanation: A macrophage presenting the allergen to a Th2 cell, which then stimulates a B cell to produce IgE, is the key sensitisation event in IgE-mediated food allergy. This primes mast cells for a rapid reaction on later exposure.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because allergen presentation to a Th2 cell drives B-cell class switching to IgE during sensitisation, preparing for an immediate reaction on re-exposure.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because neutrophils do not produce allergen-specific IgE in the sensitisation phase of IgE-mediated allergy.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because complement activation and delayed eosinophilic infiltration describe a different inflammatory process, not the classic IgE sensitisation pathway.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because mast cells do not produce IgE; they bind IgE after it is made by B cells following allergen presentation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the stem describes an IgE-mediated allergy with prior sensitisation, not direct non-IgE-mediated disease on first exposure.
